title: Implement a 'Toggle Mute' Keyboard Shortcut over Two Sessions
description: FocusCast Studio is a desktop media application for streaming and recording. Users have requested a simple keyboard shortcut to quickly toggle the mute status of the default audio input. This task requires implementing the feature incrementally across two separate development sessions. The first session will focus on the backend state management and command logic. The second session will connect this logic to the user interface by handling the keyboard input and providing visual feedback.

project_spec.name: FocusCast Studio
project_spec.description:
FocusCast Studio is an all-in-one desktop media workstation designed to streamline the daily workflow of content creators, lecturers, and knowledge workers who routinely juggle screen recordings, quick annotations, voice-overs, and file management tasks. Within a single cohesive application the user can capture video, trim clips, attach notes, and instantly drag-drop finished assets into project folders or directly into third-party collaboration suites. A rich, MVVM-driven GUI interface exposes keyboard-centric command palettes, customizable themes, and a settings pane that can be summoned from anywhere via global shortcuts—making repetitive media tasks dramatically faster.

Built on a monolithic C codebase, FocusCast Studio embeds an event-driven dispatcher, a Command Pattern action bus, and a compact State Machine that tracks capture, edit, render, and publish stages. The same binary also hosts a lightweight plug-in loader so power users can extend import/export formats without leaving the unified executable, preserving tight in-memory communication and maximizing performance on resource-constrained workstations. The result is a productivity-first desktop media tool that launches instantly, keeps context switching to a minimum, and centralizes all user data in a single project file for effortless backup and archival.
dependencies: GTK 4 (GUI toolkit with drag-drop and theming support)
libadwaita (optional modern GTK widgets, theme helpers)
libxml2 (plugin manifest & MVVM view description parsing)
dlopen / libdl (runtime plugin system, Command Pattern hooks)
